unit.title: Perform basic hair and scalp treatments

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Why do you carry out a consultation before a hair and scalp treatment?
options: To decide how much to charge for the products used on the day
To fill in time while the steamer heats up
To show the client the price list for other services
To find the client's needs and choose the right treatment

questions.stem: How do you test the porosity of a client's hair?
options: Pull a single hair from the root and look at the bulb
Slide your fingers along a strand from end to root and feel for roughness
Smell the hair to check for past chemical treatments
Wet the whole scalp and time how many minutes it takes to dry under a hood

questions.stem: What does an elasticity test tell you about the hair?
options: How strong the inner part of the hair is
How much natural colour the hair has
How many hairs grow in each square centimetre of scalp
How oily the client's scalp is

questions.stem: In an elasticity test, a wet strand stretches a long way and does not spring back. What does this show?
options: The hair is healthy and strong
The hair needs a stronger relaxer
The hair is weak and needs a protein treatment
The hair is oily and needs a clarifying shampoo

questions.stem: What does a protein treatment mainly do?
options: Adds oil to the scalp to stop dandruff forming
Helps to strengthen weak or damaged hair
Changes the natural colour of the hair
Makes the hair grow faster from the follicle

questions.stem: Hair that is dry, rough and brittle, but still has good elasticity, mainly needs which kind of treatment?
options: A strong protein treatment every day
A clarifying shampoo with no conditioner after it
A chemical relaxer to smooth it down
A moisturising deep conditioning treatment

questions.stem: What can happen if a client has too many protein treatments?
options: The hair can become stiff, dry and break easily
The hair will turn a lighter colour
The scalp will stop making natural oil for good
The hair will change from coily to straight

questions.stem: What does a clarifying shampoo do?
options: Adds colour to the hair until the next wash
Straightens the hair by breaking its bonds
Removes a build-up of products, oils and minerals
Coats the hair with a heavy layer of oil to protect it

questions.stem: Why is a conditioner usually slightly acidic (acid-balanced)?
options: So that it will lighten the natural colour
So that it opens the cuticle as wide as possible
So that it helps smooth and close the cuticle
So that it removes all oil from the scalp

questions.stem: A client has small, dry, white flakes on the scalp and shoulders, with no redness or sores. What is this most likely to be?
options: Dandruff
Head lice
Ringworm
Impetigo

questions.stem: Which product is the right choice for a client with ordinary dandruff?
options: A colour-depositing shampoo
An anti-dandruff shampoo, used as the maker says
A relaxer, to dry the scalp out
A heavy grease rubbed into the scalp several times a day

questions.stem: During a consultation you find live head lice and eggs (nits). What should you do?
options: Carry on with the treatment, then comb out the lice
Use a strong steam treatment to kill the lice
Finish the treatment, then use the same tools on the next client straight away
Stop, explain kindly, refer her to a pharmacist and disinfect the tools

questions.stem: Which client should NOT be given a scalp massage?
options: A client who feels stressed after work
A client with a dry scalp and no sores
A client who wants to relax before a blow-dry
A client with open cuts or sores on the scalp

questions.stem: Why should you avoid a firm scalp massage just before a relaxer or colour service?
options: It makes the chemical work too slowly
It makes the hair much too greasy to section and comb through
It can irritate the scalp so the chemical burns or stings
It will change the client's natural curl pattern

questions.stem: Which massage movement is a light, slow stroking used to begin and end a scalp massage?
options: Petrissage
Effleurage
Tapotement
Friction

questions.stem: What is petrissage?
options: A kneading movement that lifts and presses the skin
A light stroking movement over the surface
A quick tapping with the fingertips
A fast shaking movement made with an electric machine

questions.stem: What is the main benefit of a scalp massage?
options: It improves blood flow to the scalp and helps the client relax
It makes the hair grow twice as fast within a week
It cures scalp infections without any products
It slowly changes grey hair back to its natural shade over a month

questions.stem: A client has a very oily scalp. How should you adjust the scalp massage?
options: Use the firmest, fastest movements you can
Keep it gentle, because firm massage can increase oil flow
Massage for twice as long as usual
Rub warm oil in firmly for a long time to break up the grease

questions.stem: How should your hands work during a scalp massage?
options: With long nails pressing into the scalp
With quick, jerky movements to wake the client up fully
With the pads of the fingers, keeping an even rhythm
With the knuckles rubbed hard on one spot

questions.stem: Why is a steamer used during a deep conditioning treatment?
options: To dry the hair as quickly as possible
To straighten the hair for good without using any chemicals
To kill head lice and their eggs
To lift the cuticle gently so the conditioner can go in

questions.stem: What water should go in a hair steamer?
options: Water mixed with shampoo so that it foams
The kind of water the maker's instructions say
Water mixed with conditioner for extra shine
Any water, filled above the maximum line

questions.stem: Before you switch on a steamer or hood dryer, what should you check?
options: The cable and plug are undamaged and your hands are dry
The client has paid for the service in full
The water is filled to the very top of the tank
The machine is placed right beside the shampoo basin for ease

questions.stem: While a client is under a steamer, what should the stylist do?
options: Leave the salon to take a lunch break
Turn the steamer to its highest setting and leave
Cover the client's face with a towel to trap the steam
Stay close, check her comfort and watch the time

questions.stem: How do you check that a warmed oil is safe before applying it to the scalp?
options: Ask the client to dip her finger in it
Pour a little straight onto the client's scalp
Test a drop on the inside of your wrist
Look at it to see if steam is rising

questions.stem: How should the oil for a hot oil treatment be warmed?
options: Over an open gas flame in a metal pot
On the hot plate of a flat iron
As the maker says, often by standing the bottle in warm water
Left in direct sunlight on the salon window sill for an hour or more

questions.stem: How do you apply a deep conditioner evenly to thick hair?
options: Put it all on the crown and leave it there
Pour it over the hair at the basin and rinse straight away
Rub it only on the scalp and leave the ends dry
Apply it in sections from roots to ends and comb through

questions.stem: How long should a deep conditioning treatment be left on the hair?
options: For the time the maker's instructions give
Until the client falls asleep in the chair
Overnight, with no cap on
For as long as the client has time to stay in the salon

questions.stem: What is the gentlest way to detangle coily natural hair before a treatment?
options: Dry and in one large section, with a fine-tooth comb, from the roots down
With conditioner, using fingers or a wide-tooth comb from the ends up
With a hot comb, pulled through in one stroke
With a stiff brush, from the roots to the ends

questions.stem: Why does coily and kinky hair often feel drier than straight hair?
options: The scalp's natural oil does not travel easily down the coils
Coily hair has no cuticle layer at all
Coily hair grows without follicles, so it gets no oil from the scalp
Coily hair holds more water inside it

questions.stem: A client wears braids. How can you care for the scalp between the braids?
options: Scratch it hard with the tail of a comb to lift off all the flakes
Pour heavy grease on it every day
Cleanse it gently and apply a light scalp product to the parts
Leave it alone until the braids are taken out

questions.stem: Miss Campbell's hairline is thinning where her braids were pulled tight. What should you advise?
options: Braid it even tighter so that the hair stays flat
Choose looser styles, and see a doctor if it does not improve
Put a relaxer on the edges every two weeks to make them lie flat
Brush the edges hard every night

questions.stem: What does a leave-in conditioner do?
options: It is rinsed out at once, before styling
It cleans the hair and scalp in the same way as a shampoo
It lightens the hair a little each time
It stays in to soften, detangle and protect

questions.stem: Which scalp condition is caught from another person and must be referred to a doctor?
options: Dandruff
A dry scalp
An oily scalp
Impetigo

questions.stem: What causes an oily scalp?
options: Too little blood flow to the scalp
The sebaceous glands making too much sebum
Using a wide-tooth comb on the hair too often each day
Wearing hats in the sun

questions.stem: What should happen to towels after each client?
options: Fold them and use them again on the next client
Hang them in the sun and reuse them that day
Put them in a covered laundry bin to be washed
Spray them with perfume and put them back

questions.stem: What is the difference between disinfecting and sterilising?
options: Disinfecting kills most germs; sterilising kills all germs and spores
Disinfecting is done with soap and water; sterilising is done with plain hot water
They mean the same thing and use the same products
Sterilising only removes dirt that you can see

questions.stem: Why should water and spilled conditioner be wiped from the floor at once?
options: So that the salon smells fresh
To stop people slipping and falling
To save the product for later
So that the floor tiles keep their shine for longer

questions.stem: How should hair treatment products be stored?
options: Open, on the shampoo basin, so they are ready
In unlabelled bottles to save space
In a hot car boot for home visits
Closed and labelled, in a cool, dry place

questions.stem: A client says her scalp is burning during a treatment. What should you do first?
options: Rinse the product off at once with cool water
Turn the steamer up higher so that the treatment ends sooner
Tell her it will pass and carry on
Add more product to the burning area

questions.stem: Why does the stylist wear gloves for some scalp treatments?
options: To keep the stylist's hands warm while working under the air conditioning
To make the treatment cheaper for the client
To protect the skin from products and stop germs spreading
To stop the client from talking during the service

questions.stem: Which home-care advice suits a client with dry natural hair?
options: Shampoo every day with a strong clarifying shampoo and skip conditioner
Use a hot flat iron every morning
Moisturise regularly and sleep with hair in a satin scarf
Avoid all conditioner and oil

questions.stem: Why do you write the treatment on the client's record card?
options: So that you can track results and plan the next visit
So that you can share it with her friends
Because the card is needed for her bank
So that the salon can raise her price each time she comes in

questions.stem: Which question helps you choose a scalp treatment?
options: Which television shows do you like to watch at night?
Does your scalp itch, flake or feel tight?
Where did you buy your shoes?
How far do you live from the salon?

questions.stem: Which water temperature is best for rinsing during a scalp treatment?
options: As hot as the stylist's hands can stand, to open the cuticle fully
Ice cold, to close the pores
Whatever comes out of the tap first
Comfortably warm, checked on your wrist and with the client

questions.stem: After a treatment, how should you dry fragile hair?
options: With the hottest setting, close to the scalp
By rubbing it hard with a towel
By pulling it tight with a round brush while drying it
Gently, with a towel blot and low to medium heat

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: Name the massage movement made by rubbing small circles on the scalp with the pads of the fingers.
What is the medical name for head lice?
What oily substance do the sebaceous glands make?
What test stretches a wet strand of hair to check its strength?
Name the machine that puts moist heat on the hair during a deep conditioning treatment.
What protein is hair mainly made of?
What is the small pocket in the skin that each hair grows from?
What is the medical name for ordinary dandruff?

essays.stem: Describe how you analyse a client's hair and scalp before a treatment, and how the results help you choose the treatment.
essays.modelAnswer: I start with questions: how the client cares for her hair, what products and chemical services she has had, and whether the scalp itches, flakes or feels tight. Then I look at and feel the hair in good light. For porosity I slide my fingers from the ends to the root: rough hair is porous and takes in products fast, so it needs moisture and a treatment that smooths the cuticle. For elasticity I gently stretch a wet strand: if it stretches a long way and does not spring back, or snaps at once, it is weak and needs protein. I note the texture (fine, medium or coarse), the density and the curl pattern, from wavy to tightly coiled. I part the hair and check the scalp for flakes, oiliness, redness, cuts or signs of infection or lice. Dry, flaky scalp needs a moisturising scalp treatment, an oily scalp a gentle, balancing one. I record it all on the record card and agree the plan.
markingPoints: Asks about hair care, products, past chemical services and scalp feelings
Porosity test and what porous hair needs
Elasticity test and when protein is needed
Notes texture, density, curl pattern and scalp condition, including contraindications
Links the results to the treatment chosen and records them

essays.stem: Explain what contraindications to hair and scalp treatments you look for, and what you do if you find one.
essays.modelAnswer: A contraindication is something that means the treatment should not go ahead, or must be changed. Before any treatment or massage I part the hair and check the whole scalp. I look for open cuts, sores, grazes or abrasions, because products and massage can cause pain and infection. I look for signs of infection or infestation, such as ringworm (round scaly patches), impetigo (weeping, crusty sores) or head lice and nits, because these spread to other people. I also ask about allergies to products and recent chemical services, and avoid firm massage just before a relaxer or colour. If the scalp is very red, swollen, or has a condition such as severe psoriasis, I do not treat it. If I find a contraindication, I stop, explain kindly and in private, without trying to diagnose, and advise the client to see a doctor or pharmacist. I record it, and I clean and disinfect all tools and change towels before the next client.
markingPoints: Explains what a contraindication is and checks the whole scalp
Cuts, sores or abrasions
Infections or infestations (ringworm, impetigo, head lice) and why they matter
Other points: allergies, inflamed scalp, recent or planned chemical service
Stops, explains kindly, refers to a doctor or pharmacist, records and disinfects

essays.stem: Describe the main movements used in a scalp massage, and explain step by step how you give one.
essays.modelAnswer: The main movements are effleurage, a light, slow stroking used to begin and end the massage and to link movements; petrissage, a slow, deeper kneading that lifts and presses the scalp; and friction, small circles with the pads of the fingers that move the scalp over the bone. First I check for contraindications, gown the client and make sure she is comfortable and that my nails are short and hands clean. I may apply a scalp product or oil if the treatment needs it. I begin with effleurage from the front hairline back to the nape. Then I use petrissage and friction, working in an even pattern over the whole scalp: front, sides, crown and nape. I keep a steady rhythm and even pressure, and ask the client if the pressure is right. I use lighter pressure for an oily or sensitive scalp. I finish with slow effleurage, then carry on with the treatment or shampoo.
markingPoints: Effleurage described correctly
Petrissage described correctly
Friction described correctly
Preparation: contraindications checked, client comfortable, clean hands and short nails
A logical order over the whole scalp, even rhythm, pressure checked and adjusted

essays.stem: Compare a protein treatment and a moisturising treatment. Say what each does, what hair needs it, and what happens if the balance is wrong.
essays.modelAnswer: A protein treatment puts protein back into hair that has lost strength. It suits hair that is weak, over-processed or stretches too far in an elasticity test, for example after relaxers, colour or a lot of heat. A moisturising treatment adds water and softening oils. It suits hair that is dry, rough, dull or brittle but still has good elasticity, which is common with coily natural hair. Hair needs a balance of both. If a client has too much protein, the hair can become stiff, hard and dry, and it snaps easily. If it has too much moisture and too little protein, the hair can feel limp, mushy and over-soft, and it stretches and breaks. So I choose the treatment from the porosity and elasticity tests, use it as the maker's instructions say, and often follow a protein treatment with a moisturising conditioner. I record what I used and plan the next treatments.
markingPoints: Protein treatment strengthens weak, over-processed hair
Moisturising treatment softens dry, brittle hair with good elasticity
Too much protein makes hair stiff, hard and liable to snap
Too much moisture makes hair limp, over-soft and stretchy
Choice based on tests, used as the maker says, and recorded

essays.stem: Describe how to give a deep conditioning treatment using a steamer, from setting up to finishing, including the safety checks.
essays.modelAnswer: I consult and analyse the hair and scalp, and check for contraindications. I clean and disinfect the station and check the steamer: the cable and plug are not damaged, it has the kind of water the maker says, filled to the right line, and my hands are dry. I gown the client with a fresh towel. I shampoo the hair and towel-dry it. I apply the deep conditioner in sections from roots to ends and comb it through gently with a wide-tooth comb. I place the steamer hood at the distance the maker gives, switch it on, and set a timer for the maker's time. I stay nearby, check that the client is comfortable and not too hot, and keep the steam away from her face. When the time is up I switch off and move the steamer away, then rinse the hair with comfortably warm water until it is clean. I towel-blot, finish the style with low to medium heat, and clean the steamer as the maker says.
markingPoints: Consultation and contraindication check first
Steamer checked: cable, plug, correct water and level, dry hands
Conditioner applied in sections from roots to ends after shampooing
Correct distance, maker's timing, client never left alone and checked for comfort
Rinsed, finished gently, steamer cleaned as the maker says

essays.stem: Explain how to give a hot oil treatment safely, step by step.
essays.modelAnswer: First I consult with the client and check the scalp for cuts, sores or infection, and ask about allergies to oils or nuts. I gown the client and protect her clothes with a fresh towel. I warm the oil as the maker says, for example by standing the bottle in a bowl of warm water, and never over a flame or in a flat iron. Before it touches the client, I test a drop on the inside of my wrist to make sure it is only comfortably warm. I part the hair into sections and apply the oil to the scalp and along the hair with an applicator bottle or my fingers. I give a gentle scalp massage with effleurage and friction. I cover the hair with a plastic cap and a warm towel, or sit the client under a warm dryer, for the time the maker gives. Then I shampoo the oil out well and condition. I wipe up any oil spills at once, because they make the floor slippery.
markingPoints: Consultation, scalp check and allergy question
Oil warmed safely as the maker says, never over a flame
Temperature tested on the inside of the wrist before use
Applied in sections with a gentle massage, covered for the maker's time
Shampooed out; spills wiped up to prevent slips

essays.stem: A client with dry, tightly coiled natural hair asks for a treatment and advice. Describe the treatment you would give and the home care you would suggest.
essays.modelAnswer: Tightly coiled hair is often dry because the scalp's natural oil does not travel easily down the coils, and it breaks easily if handled roughly. After the consultation and tests, I would pre-soften the hair with conditioner and detangle it gently in small sections, using my fingers and a wide-tooth comb from the ends up to the roots. I would use a gentle, moisturising shampoo, then apply a moisturising deep conditioner in sections and use a steamer or a plastic cap for the time the maker says. After rinsing I would apply a leave-in conditioner and seal it with a light oil or cream. I would avoid high heat and tight styles. For home care, I would advise her to moisturise regularly, detangle only when the hair is damp and conditioned, sleep in a satin scarf or on a satin pillowcase, wear loose protective styles, and come back for regular treatments.
markingPoints: Explains why coily hair is dry and fragile
Gentle detangling in small sections, ends up, with conditioner
Moisturising shampoo and deep conditioner, with steam or cap for the maker's time
Leave-in and sealing product; avoids high heat and tight styles
Clear home care: moisturise, satin scarf, loose protective styles, regular treatments

essays.stem: Compare dandruff, a dry scalp and an oily scalp. Give the signs of each and the treatment, and say when you would refer the client to a doctor.
essays.modelAnswer: Dandruff shows as small white or greyish flakes that fall onto the shoulders, sometimes with mild itching. It is not caught from other people. It is treated with an anti-dandruff shampoo and treatment used as the maker says, with regular washing. A dry scalp feels tight and itchy, with fine, small, dry flakes, often after harsh shampoo, sun or too little moisture. It is treated with a gentle, moisturising shampoo and a moisturising scalp treatment or light oil. An oily scalp looks shiny, the hair goes limp and greasy soon after washing, and flakes may be yellow and stick to the scalp. It needs a gentle, balancing shampoo, regular washing and only light massage, because firm massage can increase oil flow. I refer the client to a doctor if the scalp is red, sore, weeping or bleeding, if there are thick scales, bald patches or signs of infection, or if the condition does not improve with salon care.
markingPoints: Dandruff: white flakes on shoulders, not infectious, anti-dandruff products
Dry scalp: tight, itchy, fine dry flakes, moisturising care
Oily scalp: shiny, greasy, sticky flakes, balancing shampoo and light massage
Treatments used as the maker says
Refers for redness, sores, weeping, bald patches, infection or no improvement

essays.stem: Explain the difference between cleaning, disinfecting and sterilising, and describe how you keep tools, towels and the work station hygienic during treatments.
essays.modelAnswer: Cleaning removes dirt, hair, product and grease with soap or detergent and water. It must be done first, because disinfectant does not work well on dirty tools. Disinfecting uses a chemical disinfectant, made up and left for the contact time the maker says, to kill most germs on tools and surfaces. Sterilising kills all germs and their spores, for example with an autoclave, and is used for tools that may break the skin. In the salon I remove hair from combs and brushes, wash them in warm soapy water, rinse and dry them, then disinfect them as the maker says and store them in a clean, closed container. I use a fresh towel and gown for each client and put used ones in a covered laundry bin. I wipe the chair, basin, trolley and steamer with disinfectant between clients. I wash my hands before and after each client. Single-use items such as caps are thrown away after one use.
markingPoints: Cleaning removes dirt and comes first
Disinfecting kills most germs, made up and left as the maker says
Sterilising kills all germs and spores
Combs and brushes cleaned, disinfected and stored covered
Fresh towels for each client, surfaces wiped, hands washed, single-use items thrown away

essays.stem: Describe the aftercare advice you give after a hair and scalp treatment, and explain why you keep a record of the treatment.
essays.modelAnswer: I explain what the treatment did and how to keep the result. I suggest suitable shampoo, conditioner and scalp products for her hair and scalp type, and tell her how often to use them, as the maker says. I advise her to avoid very hot water, harsh shampoo, high heat and tight styles, and to protect the hair from strong sun and sea water. For dry or natural hair I suggest regular moisturising and a satin scarf at night. I tell her to contact the salon if the scalp itches or becomes sore. I recommend when to come back, for example a course of treatments. On the record card I write the date, the analysis and test results, any contraindications, the products and heat used, the timing, the result and the advice given. Records show what works for that client, help any stylist plan the next visit, and protect the client and the salon if there is a complaint or reaction.
markingPoints: Explains the result and recommends suitable home products
Advises on water, heat, styles, sun and sea water
Tells the client to report any soreness, and when to return
Records date, tests, products, timing, result and advice
Explains why records matter (planning, safety, complaints)

practical1.title: Hair and scalp analysis and a deep conditioning treatment with a steamer
practical1.brief: Work in pairs inside your group (one group of three if needed), on members who agree to be models, in the Centre's salon. Each member consults with a partner, carries out a porosity test and an elasticity test, checks the scalp for contraindications, and fills in a record card with the results and the chosen treatment. Then each member gives their partner a deep conditioning treatment: shampoo, apply the conditioner in sections from roots to ends, check the steamer and place it as the maker says, time the treatment, rinse and finish with low to medium heat. Swap roles so that every member gives and receives a treatment, or uses a training head if a member cannot be a model. Photos show only hair and the work area, never faces. Clean and disinfect the station and steamer at the end and hand in the record cards with the photos.
materials: Steamer, checked and filled as the maker says
Gowns, fresh towels and plastic caps
Gentle shampoo and a deep conditioner, with the maker's instructions
Wide-tooth combs, sectioning clips, applicator brush and bowl
Cleaning and disinfecting products for tools and surfaces
photos: The station set up with clean tools and the steamer checked
A porosity or elasticity test being done on a strand
The completed record card for each model
Conditioner being applied in sections from roots to ends
The model's hair under the steamer, with the timer showing
The station, tools and steamer cleaned
checklist: Asked suitable consultation questions and checked the scalp for cuts, sores, infection or lice
Did the porosity and elasticity tests correctly and recorded the results
Chose a suitable treatment from the results and explained why
Checked the steamer cable, plug and water before use, with dry hands
Applied the conditioner evenly in sections and timed it as the maker says
Stayed with the client and checked her comfort under the steamer
Rinsed thoroughly at a comfortable temperature and finished gently
Gave aftercare advice and cleaned, then disinfected, the tools and station
safety: Check electrical equipment before use; keep cables away from water and use it with dry hands
Never leave a client alone under a steamer; keep steam away from the face
Do not treat over cuts, sores, infection or lice; refer instead
Wipe up water and product spills at once to prevent slips
Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules

practical2.title: Scalp massage and hot oil treatment on natural and textured hair
practical2.brief: As a group, plan and give a scalp massage and hot oil treatment suited to natural and textured hair. Use members who agree to be models (photos show hair, hands and scalp only), or a training head for parts that do not need a real scalp. Together, fill in a short treatment plan naming the oil, how it will be warmed safely, the massage movements and the aftercare. Each member then gives part of the service while the assessor watches: one checks the scalp and asks about nut or oil allergies, one detangles gently in small sections, one warms the oil as the maker says and tests it on the inside of the wrist, and each member gives the massage (effleurage, petrissage and friction) on one area of the scalp. Cover the hair for the maker's time, shampoo out, apply a leave-in conditioner and finish in a protective style such as twists. Clean the area and wipe up any oil at once.
materials: Treatment oil suited to natural hair, with the maker's instructions
Bowl of warm water for warming the bottle, and a thermometer if the Centre has one
Applicator bottles, wide-tooth combs and sectioning clips
Plastic caps, gowns and fresh towels
Moisturising shampoo, leave-in conditioner and a light sealing cream
Treatment plan sheet and record cards
photos: Gentle detangling of a small section
The wrist test on the warmed oil
Oil being applied to the scalp in sections
A massage movement on the scalp (hands and hair only)
The hair covered with a cap during processing
The finished protective style, and the clean work area
checklist: Checked the scalp and asked about allergies before starting
Detangled gently in small sections from the ends up
Warmed the oil safely as the maker says and tested it on the inside of the wrist
Applied the oil evenly to the scalp and hair
Used correct effleurage, petrissage and friction with even pressure, checking the client's comfort
Timed the processing and shampooed the oil out well
Finished in a neat protective style without pulling the edges
Gave suitable home-care advice and cleaned the area, wiping spills at once
safety: Never warm oil over a flame or on a hot tool; test it on the wrist before it touches the client
Ask about nut and oil allergies; stop if the scalp stings or reddens
Do not massage over cuts, sores or infection
Wipe up oil at once, because it makes floors and chairs slippery
Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules
